steps.say: A pictogram uses symbols. The key tells you what one symbol means.

figure.title: Books read
figure.alt: Pictogram of books read. Each symbol means 2 books. Monday: 3 symbols. Tuesday: 5 symbols.

steps.say: Each symbol means 2 books. Monday has 3 symbols.
A bar chart uses bars. Read across from the top of a bar to the scale.

figure.alt: Bar chart of favourite colours: Red 6, Blue 10, Green 4.

steps.say: The Blue bar reaches 10, so 10 children chose blue.

check.prompt: Each symbol means 2 children. How many children chose cats?
hints: Count the symbols in the Cats row.
Count in 2s, one step for each symbol.

figure.title: Favourite pets
figure.alt: Pictogram of favourite pets. Each symbol means 2 children. Cats: 4 symbols. Fish: 2 symbols. Birds: 3 symbols.

check.prompt: How many more children chose football than swimming?
hints: Read the Football bar and the Swimming bar.
Take the smaller number away from the bigger one.

figure.alt: Bar chart of favourite sports: Football 14, Swimming 8, Badminton 10.
